title: Hansard domain semantic profile v2

structural_dependencies.policy: These frozen v1 schemas remain byte-identical structural dependencies; they do not declare the core version or the Hansard domain profile.

source_model.unit: A source-linked text-bearing contribution, proceedings section, dated record, entity or sitting-day concept.
source_model.identifiers: Stable route-derived Hansard IRIs and assertion IDs; retain existing source identities across regeneration.
source_model.evidence: Every relationship assertion retains its source artifact digest, field pointer, source URL and retrieval timestamp where available.
source_model.relationship_graph: Generated assertions are evidence-bearing projections of captured sources and documented literal matching rules. They do not establish substantive agreement or causal relationships.
source_model.navigation: The virtual root index is a Reader navigation record, marked core_role navigation, and is not a Markdown concept or semantic domain assertion.

competency_questions: Which Commons and Lords contribution records were available on a selected sitting day?
What mentions in earlier sittings can I follow from this contribution, by entity and facet?
Which person is named, which office is referenced and who held that office on the day?
Can I open an official source for each result and see whether it still matches the captured version?
Can the same result drive a spoken answer, accessible table and source-linked chart?
interpretation_limits: Name and alias matches are discovery leads; they do not establish that a passage is substantively about the matched entity.
The fixed alias profile has no measured recall across the archive.
Same-day matches in separate sections have unknown order.
A reference to an office and a dated appointment record have distinct identities and assertion types.
A claim, opinion or forecast records what was said in a source context; it does not establish the claim as fact.
Coverage in a bundle is limited to the exact captured dates and source completeness recorded in its verification receipt.
